name: Saint Clare
history: A young noblewoman of Assisi who, moved by the preaching of Saint Francis, left her family by night in 1212 to give herself to Christ in poverty. At San Damiano she founded the Poor Ladies, now the Poor Clares, and for over forty years guarded their poverty with great firmness. She wrote the first rule for women approved by a pope.
life: Clare Offreduccio heard Francis preach and resolved to follow Christ as he did. On the night after Palm Sunday 1212 she slipped out of her family’s house and went to the little church of the Portiuncula, where Francis cut her hair and received her vows. Her family tried to bring her back by force, but she held to the altar. Her sister Agnes soon joined her, and later her widowed mother. At San Damiano the sisters lived enclosed, in strict poverty, by prayer and the work of their hands. Clare fought for years for the privilege of owning nothing at all, and her own rule was approved by Innocent IV two days before she died. Tradition holds that when soldiers attacked the convent in 1240 she faced them with the Blessed Sacrament and they fled. Too ill to go to Mass one Christmas, she is said to have seen and heard it from her bed, and so is patron of television. She was canonised in 1255.
prayerTo: Saint Clare, you held fast to Christ poor and crucified and found in Him all your riches. Pray that I may be free of the things I cling to, and find my joy in God. Watch over the Poor Clares and all enclosed nuns, and make my own home a place of prayer and peace. Amen.
penance: Give away something you own and do not need today, and pray for an enclosed community of nuns near you.
meditation: Clare urged Saint Agnes of Prague to gaze upon Christ, consider Him and contemplate Him. Spend a few minutes today simply looking at a crucifix or an image of Christ.
